summary: Lean capped finders for the 8 collision-search angles that never ran (patents, citation chase, non-English, grey, venues, MARL compatibility, method/theory)

candidates.title: Method for generating a traffic control signal (EP3594920A1)
candidates.venue: EPO patent application, Siemens Mobility GmbH
candidates.overlap: This is the closest patent to C4's architecture that we found. It inserts virtual detector signals in front of an existing adaptive or actuated signal controller. Those signals come from upstream detections 400-600 m out and a NARX neural-network prediction of platoon arrivals, and they replace or add to the real detector inputs. The stated aim is to give vehicles more stable GLOSA and time-to-green/red advice, with 20-35 s of foresight. That is the same building block as C4: a transform on the detector input that sits in front of a controller left unchanged, used to make signal timing work with speed advisory.
candidates.does_not: The controller it fronts is conventional, not a frozen learned DQN, so it does not touch the learned signal. The input is not compensated for advised or gliding vehicles that disappear from halting counts; the problem it solves is foresight, not the self-defeating forecast. It has no speed-binned count adapter and no per-signal calibration of an adapter with both policies frozen. It does not model that published forecasts change the controller's input.

candidates.title: Method and arrangement for predicting switching times of a signal group of a signal system for controlling traffic flow (WO2021110370A1)
candidates.venue: WIPO patent application, Siemens Mobility GmbH
candidates.overlap: It uses two neural networks to predict switching times of traffic-actuated or adaptive signal groups from detector values. The first network fills in missing or delayed status data; the second, a recurrent network, predicts switching times. It outputs a probability distribution for the remaining time in the current signal state, more than 120 s ahead, and in the vehicle the forecast drives optimal-speed advice. That matches C3's uncertainty-aware ML forecast for a non-fixed signal used for GLOSA.
candidates.does_not: The signal it forecasts is actuated or adaptive, not an RL or DQN policy. It does not split the forecast into exact time-to-green in determined yellow plus a quantile forecast. Training is open-loop on historical forecast-versus-actual switching times, not on logs recorded while forecasts were published. It explicitly does not model vehicles acting on the forecast changing detector inputs (no C2 feedback), and it has no signal-side adapter.

candidates.title: Traffic signal timing estimation using an artificial neural network model (US20170169705A1)
candidates.venue: USPTO patent application, Nissan North America / Nissan Motor Co
candidates.overlap: An ANN or SVR is trained on signal-controller logs to predict the remaining green or red time of vehicle-actuated signals, and the signal state when the vehicle arrives. Its inputs include loop-detector vehicle counts, elapsed phase time, previous phase durations and internal controller state. An autonomous vehicle uses the prediction to adjust speed and avoid stopping. That is a learned SPaT forecaster for a demand-responsive signal, conditioned on the same kind of count state the paper's DQN sees.
candidates.does_not: It has no quantile or confidence output and does not target a learned or RL signal controller. It does not handle feedback: the patent does not consider that vehicles acting on the estimate change detector counts and therefore the timing. It does not train on forecast-published logs, has no exact determined-yellow component and no signal-side adapter.

candidates.title: Traffic signal state prediction correction and real-time probe data validation (WO2020086615A1 / US10878693B2)
candidates.venue: WIPO / USPTO patent, Traffic Technology Services Inc
candidates.overlap: It emulates the field controller with its timing parameters to make deterministic baseline signal-change predictions, then corrects them using real-time controller data (for example clock drift above about 3 s). Before broadcasting to vehicles, it checks the predictions against GPS probe data from vehicles crossing the stop line. This is a building block for the exact part of C3: running the controller's own logic to get deterministic time-to-change before publishing.
candidates.does_not: The prediction uses controller emulation, not ML, and the patent says nothing about RL or learned signal policies. It gives no confidence, probability or quantiles. It does not discuss vehicles acting on the published prediction changing detector actuations or timing, so it does not cover the self-defeating mechanism, and it has no detector or count adapter.

candidates.title: Prediction of traffic signal state changes (US9396657B1) and Hybrid distributed prediction of traffic signal state changes (US10008113B2 / WO2017003793A1)
candidates.venue: USPTO / WIPO patents, Traffic Technology Services Inc
candidates.overlap: Not opened; this is based on search snippets only. Per the snippets, these TTS patents predict state changes for non-fixed (actuated or adaptive) signals and broadcast them to vehicles for fuel efficiency. They may estimate the probability that a phase is called or extended and attach a confidence measure, said to matter especially for adaptive signals. That would be a building block for C3's uncertainty-aware SPaT.
candidates.does_not: The snippets do not mention learned or RL controllers, closed-loop training on forecast-published logs, the feedback of advised vehicles on detector inputs, or a signal-side adapter. Open the documents before citing them for probability or confidence.

candidates.title: Method and device for predicting the time remaining of a signal phase (US 12,148,293)
candidates.overlap: Not opened; per the search snippet, a combination neural network outputs a prediction of the remaining time of a signal phase for signal groups. That is an ML-based time-to-change forecaster, a building block for C3.
candidates.does_not: From the snippet, nothing shows a learned or RL controller, a quantile or exact hybrid, closed-loop training, publish-feedback, or a signal-side adapter. Assignee and details not verified.

candidates.title: Traffic light prediction (EP3671687A1)
candidates.overlap: Not opened; per the search snippet, the predicted traffic-light state includes a recommended speed for reaching the light on green and/or a probability of reaching it on green. That links an uncertain SPaT forecast directly to speed advice, a building block for C3's quantile forecast feeding GLOSA.
candidates.does_not: From the snippet, nothing shows a learned or RL controller, closed-loop or publish-feedback training, or compensation of the signal's detector inputs. Assignee and details not verified.

candidates.title: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for integrated and networked adaptive traffic signal control (US9818297B2)
candidates.overlap: A patented learned (MARL) adaptive signal controller: the kind of controller the city upgrades to in C1.
candidates.does_not: Based on the search result only, it has no SPaT forecasting for vehicles, no eco-driving fleet, no publish-feedback mechanism and no input adapter.

candidates.title: Smart and scalable urban signal networks: methods and systems for adaptive traffic signal control (US20140368358A1, SURTRAC)
candidates.overlap: A schedule-driven adaptive controller that sits in front of the field signal controller and allocates green time in real time. It is the commercial lineage (Rapid Flow) of adaptive signals whose timing is not known in advance.
candidates.does_not: Based on the search result only, it is not a learned DQN controller. It has no quantile SPaT for an eco-driving fleet, no publish-feedback analysis and no speed-binned count adapter.

candidates.title: Speed Advisory System Using Real-Time Actuated Traffic Light Phase Length Prediction
candidates.overlap: Uses advanced-detector data to predict the current green length of semi- or fully-actuated signals and gives connected vehicles PASS/WAIT advice. The snippet reports about 95% prediction accuracy and up to 30% fuel saving. It is a GLOSA-plus-prediction pipeline for demand-responsive signals.
candidates.does_not: Based on the search snippet only, it does not cover a learned signal, a quantile or exact hybrid, closed-loop or publish-feedback effects on detectors, or a signal-side adapter.

candidates.title: Final Thesis (University of Southampton, eprint 502165): GLOSA paired with responsive traffic control systems [exact title not retrieved, page returned 403]
candidates.venue: University of Southampton PhD thesis (ePrints Soton)
candidates.overlap: C1/C2. The search snippet states that GLOSA becomes a detriment when paired with responsive traffic control systems, which are widespread, and that this greatly reduces where GLOSA helps. That is the same problem as the paper's staged-upgrade loss: a speed-advisory fleet loses its benefit once signals respond to traffic. The setting is adjacent: responsive (non-learned) controllers and rule-based GLOSA rather than a frozen DQN signal and a PPO fleet.
candidates.does_not: It was not verified to use learned policies on either side, a halting-count mechanism, publish versus shadow forecasts, or a two-sided interface fix. The page returned 403, so the title, mechanism and any proposed remedy are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: TRC-30 paper 296: integrating actuated signal control with queue-based GLOSA (Q-GLOSA) using loop-detector and probe queue estimation
candidates.overlap: C2/C3 building block. It combines an actuated (traffic-responsive) signal policy with a queue-aware GLOSA whose trajectories use real-time queue estimates from loop detectors and probes. That is the queue/detector coupling between an advisory fleet and a responsive signal.
candidates.does_not: The signal is not learned or frozen, the GLOSA fleet is not learned, there is no forecast trained on forecast-published closed-loop logs, no count adapter in front of the signal, and no self-defeating-forecast analysis.

candidates.title: Enabling GLOSA through Domain Knowledge Aware SPaT Prediction and Queue Length Aware Trajectory Optimization
candidates.venue: USDOT / Morgan State National Transportation Center (SMARTER) report
candidates.overlap: C3 building block. It predicts SPaT for actuated signals with a hybrid of deep learning and controller domain logic, so that predictions follow the controller's logic, and pairs this with queue-length-aware GLOSA trajectory optimization. This resembles the hybrid exact plus learned forecast feeding a queue-aware eco-approach.
candidates.does_not: The target is actuated controllers, not a learned DQN signal. The forecast is not described as trained closed-loop on forecast-published logs, and there is no publish-versus-shadow feedback, no signal-side adapter, and no frozen learned fleet.

candidates.title: Reinforcement Learning Approaches for Traffic Signal Control Under Missing Data
candidates.overlap: C4 building block. It puts an input-side transformation (state imputation) in front of an RL signal policy when detectors do not observe parts of the traffic state, so the signal policy can act on a corrected observation.
candidates.does_not: It handles missing sensors, not systematic undercounting caused by gliding eco-driving vehicles that stay above the halting threshold. The imputation is learned, not a physical 2-parameter speed-binned adapter, and it does not pair the signal with a learned fleet or study forecast feedback.

candidates.title: Cooperative signal and vehicle control in mixed traffic environment using model-guided reinforcement learning (SVCC)
candidates.overlap: It pairs learned signal agents with learned CAV eco-driving agents (the assignment's pairing criterion). A queuing model gives advisory speeds to the eco-driving agents through a shaping reward.
candidates.does_not: The two policies are trained together (the CoTV-style joint-training category), so it has no staged upgrade, no frozen policies, no SPaT forecast of a learned signal, no count adapter, and no self-defeating-forecast mechanism.

candidates.title: Sim2Signal: Sim-to-Real Benchmarks for Traffic Signal Control
candidates.overlap: A deployment-gap benchmark: one shared pretrained signal checkpoint per network and controller pair is carried through pretrain, train and deploy stages on LibSignal (SUMO/CityFlow). It is close in spirit to adapting around a fixed learned signal.
candidates.does_not: No learned vehicle fleet, no input-count adapter, and no SPaT forecasting.

candidates.title: A Graph-Based Control Interface for Traffic Signals on Heterogeneous Road Networks
candidates.overlap: A PPO signal-control interface that runs one trained policy across unseen geometries and city graphs, and reports that a shift in signal coverage exposes the policy's sensitivity. This is an input-side shift for a fixed learned signal.
candidates.does_not: No adapter in front of a frozen policy, no vehicle-side learned fleet, and no forecast.

candidates.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Reinforcement Learning based Adaptive Traffic Signal Control
candidates.overlap: A robustness evaluation of frozen RL signal controllers under perturbed conditions. It is related to how a learned signal degrades when its inputs change, for example because of eco-driving vehicles.
candidates.does_not: Content not inspected. Its title shows no fleet, no forecast and no adapter.

candidates.does_not: Speed information is built into the RL state at training time. There is no adapter in front of a frozen, already-trained signal, no eco-driving or GLOSA fleet, and no forecast feedback.

candidates.does_not: Not opened. The title and the 'advised vehicles alter arrivals/conflict' claim come only from a search-engine summary and may be synthesis. Open this first if more budget is available.

candidates.title: Using Reinforcement Learning to Combine Green Light Optimised Speed Advisory and Responsive Traffic Control Systems with Non-Autonomous Vehicles: Effects of Imperfect Training and Incomplete Information (PhD thesis, William Paine, University of Southampton)
candidates.venue: University of Southampton doctoral thesis (ePrints Soton 502165)
candidates.overlap: This is the closest grey-literature hit. The abstract snippets I saw say that GLOSA becomes a detriment when paired with responsive traffic control systems (RTCs), that RTCs cannot give accurate long-term signal plans without mitigation, and that RL frameworks are built to combine GLOSA with RTCs for connected non-autonomous vehicles. 'Imperfect training and incomplete information' sits close to our no-retraining, frozen-policy setting. It shares the problem (C1: the speed-advice benefit collapses once signals become responsive) and probably the remedy direction (C5: repair the GLOSA-signal interface). The full text returned HTTP 403 for both the PDF and the landing page, so I could not check four things: whether the RTC is a learned (RL) controller or a conventional one (MOVA/SCOOT/actuated); whether either policy is frozen; whether the mechanism is the detector/queue feedback of C2; and whether it uses a signal-side adapter (C4) or a quantile forecast (C3).
candidates.does_not: From the snippets alone, nothing shows both learned policies held frozen, a two-sided interface (fleet-side forecast plus signal-side count adapter), a self-defeating-forecast analysis through halting counts, or a pre-registered non-inferiority/crossed-bootstrap design. The full text must be read before the paper is submitted. This is the top-priority collision to check.

candidates.title: MAVEN - Managing Automated Vehicles Enhances Network (H2020 project 690727): infrastructure-assisted platoon negotiation, GLOSA and negotiation-driven adaptive traffic control
candidates.overlap: In this EU project, GLOSA is coupled bi-directionally with an adaptive signal controller. Vehicles send trip details to the signal, which uses them to improve its queue-length estimate, and the signal plan is updated through negotiation. That is a signal-side input correction built from vehicle information, a building block related to C4 (repairing what the signal 'sees' about the advised vehicles) and to the two-sided framing of C5.
candidates.does_not: The controller is conventional/optimisation-based, not a frozen learned controller. The fleet policy is not a learned PPO policy, and the design is co-designed and negotiated rather than retrofitted with both policies frozen. There is no forecast quantile model, no self-defeating-forecast analysis, and no non-inferiority statistics.

candidates.title: STAMP: Scalable Task And Model-agnostic Collaborative Perception
candidates.overlap: A two-sided interface between independently trained, heterogeneous agents (connected vehicles). Lightweight adapter-reverter pairs on both sides map each agent's BEV features into a shared protocol domain and back, so existing agents can collaborate without joint retraining and without sharing model details. It is the closest general analogue of C4/C5's 'repair the interface on both sides around existing learned models', and it targets traffic.
candidates.does_not: Perception only, with no control loop, no learned signal controller, no forecast and no feedback or performative effect. Adapters are trained per agent toward a common protocol. The abstract does not explicitly say the agents' models stay frozen. There is no staged upgrade of one population, no self-defeating forecast, no non-inferiority design.

candidates.title: One is Plenty: A Polymorphic Feature Interpreter for Immutable Heterogeneous Collaborative Perception (PolyInter)
candidates.overlap: Explicitly targets 'immutable' heterogeneous agents (fixed perception networks that cannot be modified). One shared interpreter, with small per-agent learnable prompts, bridges the semantic gap, so a new agent type joins by training about 1.4% of parameters. It is an adapter between frozen, independently trained vehicle agents (traffic). Per the search result it is compared against PnPDA and MPDA, described as the only earlier interpreters for immutable heterogeneous collaboration.
candidates.does_not: One-sided: only the ego agent interprets the others' features. Perception, not control. No closed loop through queues or signals, no forecast, no upgrade-induced loss of benefit.

candidates.title: BOLT: Online Lightweight Adaptation for Preparation-Free Heterogeneous Cooperative Perception
candidates.overlap: Independently trained single-agent detectors with no pre-deployment coordination. The ego model stays frozen, and a 0.9M-parameter online adapter (ego-as-teacher distillation) aligns neighbours' features at runtime. Same 'no joint training, no retraining of deployed models, lightweight calibrated adapter' framing as C4, in V2V traffic (DAIR-V2X, OPV2V).
candidates.does_not: One-sided, perception only, no learned controller or control loop, no forecast or performative effect, no two-population upgrade staging.

candidates.title: TaCA: Upgrading Your Visual Foundation Model with Task-agnostic Compatible Adapter
candidates.overlap: Upgrade-compatibility setting: when the upstream foundation model is upgraded, a parameter-efficient compatible adapter lets the frozen downstream modules keep working without retraining. This is the general ML analogue of C1's 'one component upgraded, the other frozen, restore compatibility with an adapter'.
candidates.does_not: Static feed-forward pipeline, not two interacting learned agent populations. No closed-loop dynamics, no performative feedback, no RL policies, no traffic. Seen via search snippet only.

candidates.title: X-Adapter: Adding Universal Compatibility of Plugins for Upgraded Diffusion Model
candidates.overlap: Same upgrade-compatibility pattern: plugins trained for the old base model are kept frozen and reused on an upgraded base model through a learned adapter, so the downstream components need no retraining.
candidates.does_not: Generative-model plugins. No interacting agents, closed loop, forecast or traffic. Seen via search snippet only.

candidates.title: MUSCLE: A Model Update Strategy for Compatible LLM Evolution
candidates.overlap: After a base-model update, downstream task adapters regress (negative flips). A compatibility adapter reduces the regression, by up to about 40% from Llama 1 to Llama 2. This is the 'upgrade one side, frozen other side loses benefit, repair with a compatibility module' story in LLMs (cf. Bansal 2019, already known).
candidates.does_not: No multi-agent interaction, no closed-loop or performative feedback, the compatibility adapter is trained on the updated side, no traffic. Seen via search snippet only.

candidates.title: Learning Translations: Emergent Communication Pretraining for Cooperative Language Acquisition (ECTL / CLAP)
candidates.overlap: A 'joiner' agent must interoperate with an existing, independently trained agent community whose emergent protocol it does not share. It learns a translator between its own protocol and the community's from a dataset of the community's interaction logs, without retraining the community. Closest MARL analogue of a translator between two independently trained populations learned from logs (cf. C3's quantile forecast trained on logs).
candidates.does_not: One-sided (only the joiner adapts). Referential and communication games, not control through a physical queue. No upgrade staging, no performative or self-defeating effect, no traffic. Seen via search snippet only.

candidates.title: Multiplayer Performative Prediction: Learning in Decision-Dependent Games
candidates.overlap: Formalizes performative feedback between several learned decision makers: the data distribution each learner sees depends on the decisions of all of them. This is the general mechanism behind C2, where the fleet's published forecast shifts the signal's input and hence the forecast target. It gives a formal model of such cross-learner feedback (relevant to C7).
candidates.does_not: Learners repeatedly retrain toward performatively stable or Nash equilibria, the opposite of the frozen-policy setting. No interface or adapter fix, no queue model, no traffic. Seen via search snippet only.

candidates.title: Performative Time-Series Forecasting (PeTS / Feature Performative-Shifting)

candidates.does_not: Single forecaster with a generic population response, not a second frozen learned controller. No signal or queue mechanism, no adapter on the other side, no traffic SPaT. Seen via search snippet only.

candidates.overlap: From the snippets: an infrastructure-to-vehicle setting where the actuated signal sends a probability distribution of the next switching time, and vehicles optimize trajectories against that distribution and update as it changes. This is a building block for C3, the distributional or quantile forecast consumed by an eco-approach fleet. It may belong to the already-known Genser or Eteifa lines; I did not check the authors.
candidates.does_not: Forecasts a rule-based actuated controller, not a learned DQN signal. The forecast is not trained closed-loop on logs where it was published, and the paper does not model how the advised vehicles change the controller's input (C2).

candidates.title: Arrangement and method for providing adaptation to queue length for traffic light assist-applications (US 11055995)
candidates.overlap: The title, seen in search results, claims queue-length adaptation of traffic-light-assist (GLOSA-type) advice. That would be a fleet-side building block next to C3 and C2: advice that depends on the queue in front of the signal.
candidates.does_not: The fetched PDF was a scanned image and its claims could not be read, so the queue adaptation is confirmed by the title only. Nothing seen suggests it models the advice feeding back into the signal's detector or queue input, or a learned signal.

candidates.title: Information Design for Regulating Traffic Flows under Uncertain Network State (Wu & Amin)
candidates.overlap: A Bayesian-persuasion analytical model: an authority designs a noisy signal sent to a fraction of travelers to steer the equilibrium flow, and the optimum is characterized in closed form against the fraction that receives the signal. It is the closest formal precedent for treating a published forecast as an information-design choice (publish vs shadow, penetration) for C7.
candidates.does_not: Covers route choice only. It has no signal timing, queues at an intersection, halting-count feedback into a signal controller, or learned policies.

candidates.title: JASSS 7(1) 1: traffic forecast and route-choice agent simulation (forecast-reacting drivers do not reach equilibrium)
candidates.venue: Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation
candidates.overlap: Per the search snippet, it shows that a traffic system where a large share of drivers react to the forecast will not reach equilibrium. This is a classic self-defeating-forecast result in traffic, in the same family as the already-known Bottom 2000.
candidates.does_not: Covers route choice, not signal SPaT. It has no queue or detector channel into a signal controller and no learned signal or fleet.

candidates.title: How Many Random Seeds? Statistical Power Analysis in Deep Reinforcement Learning Experiments (Colas, Sigaud, Oudeyer)
candidates.overlap: Standard reference for seed-level t-tests and bootstrap confidence-interval tests and for choosing the number of seeds in deep RL comparisons. It supports how C6 sizes its seed panels.
candidates.does_not: Covers a single learned population per arm. It has no crossed two-population bootstrap, no non-inferiority margin, no pre-registration and no traffic.
